question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Post-stimulus washout time-course of AP-1 occupancy and chromatin
ideas.description: After a defined AP-1-inducing stimulus, track c-Jun/c-Fos/ATF3 occupancy (CUT&RUN or ChIP-seq), chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq), and transcription (RNA-seq) at many time points after withdrawal. Memory is supported if AP-1 binding and enhancer opening persist after transcripts return to baseline, and the persistence window is quantified per locus.

ideas.title: Inducible AP-1 degradation during distinct phases of the memory window
ideas.description: Use an auxin-inducible degron or dTAG system on Fos or Jun to deplete AP-1 at different times: during priming, during the quiescent interval, and at re-stimulation. If memory is AP-1-dependent, depletion during the maintenance phase should abolish the enhanced or faster re-induction of memory genes, while depletion only during priming should have a different effect.

ideas.title: Motif and enhancer perturbation with sufficiency tests
ideas.description: Use base editing or CRISPR deletion to mutate AP-1 motifs within enhancers that carry the memory signature, and measure whether priming-dependent faster or stronger re-induction is lost while the first response is preserved. Complement this with dCas9-tethered c-Jun, Fos, or p300 at silent sites to test whether AP-1 recruitment alone is sufficient to install a memory-like state.

ideas.title: Single-cell lineage tracing of AP-1 memory heritability
ideas.description: Combine a live AP-1 transcriptional reporter with lineage barcoding, then pulse stimulate and follow cells over several divisions without further stimulus. Measure whether daughter cells inherit the primed state and its re-inducibility, and whether the memory is a stable cell-intrinsic state or a population-level drift that dissipates.

ideas.title: In vivo tagging and recall challenge of stimulus-experienced cells
ideas.description: Label cells that experienced an AP-1-inducing stimulus in vivo using a Fos-based activity tag such as Fos-CreER or TRAP, then challenge the animal or transplant the tagged cells and measure the recall response. Test necessity by ablating or AP-1-depleting the tagged population and checking whether the enhanced recall response disappears, which would connect the molecular memory to a functional outcome.
